response.sql: WITH per_patient AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.ALP * 1.0 / l.GPT) AS avg_ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory x WHERE x.ID = p.ID AND x.`U-PRO` = '-') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX) SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_PT, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ALP_GPT_ratio FROM per_patient GROUP BY SEX

assumptions.assumption: Patients whose U-PRO is NULL in some records are not excluded; only an explicit '-' value excludes a patient.
A record with GPT = 0 or NULL gives a NULL ratio (division by zero returns NULL in SQLite), so it is ignored in the ratio average. PT is averaged independently of the ratio.
SEX is grouped as stored, so blank and NULL values each form their own group and are not merged or relabeled.
